## 21.4Riskculture

Risk culture comprises the shared norms and behaviours determining how risk is actually treated, as distinct from how policy states it should be. The Group assesses its culture annually using employee survey results, Speak Up volumes and themes, incident and issue self-identification rates, RCSA challenge outcomes, exception and acceptance volumes, and behavioural indicators drawn from performance and conduct data.

A high proportion of issues identified by the business itself, rather than by audit or regulators, is treated as a positive indicator. A low incident reporting volume is investigated rather than celebrated, on the basis that it more often indicates under-reporting than em absence of incidents.

## 21.5 Speak Up

All individuals may raise concerns confidentially, and anonymously where they choose, through the Group Speak Up channel operated independently of line management. Concerns relating to risk, control, conduct or compliance are routed to the appropriate function for investigation, with oversight by the Audit Committee. Retaliation against any person raising a concern in good faith is a serious disciplinary matter, whether or not the concern is ultimately substantiated.
